summary: Eugène Burnouf was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy around 1822–1832, worked at the Court of Appeal of Paris, and taught at the Collège de France (1832–1852).

Eugène Denis worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a Ph.D. from the University of Paris by 1976. He served as a CNRS research scholar (1961–1986) and held posts at Bangkok University and Chulalongkorn University (Professor, 1976).

Eugène Henri Guillaume Edgard Monseur was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Charles Michel and earned his doctorate at the University of Liège (~1879–1884). He was Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Grammar at Université libre de Bruxelles (1888–1912).

Eugène Jacquet was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Sinology. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, Antoine-Léonard Chézy, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, Pierre-Amédée Jaubert, and Eugène Burnouf.

Eugène Obermiller specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Dondub Buddhayin, he held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Culture, the Institute of Oriental Studies, and the University of Chicago.
Eugène Pittard worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Geneva from around 1894 to 1899 and later held a post there from circa 1916 to 1949.

Eugène Tisserant studied in the fields of history, archaeology, and religious studies. His education included studies at Lycée Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1905–1908), and the École du Louvre (~1906–1908).

Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault was an Indologist who studied at Petit Séminaire de Saint-Nicolas-du-Chardonnet and under Eugène Burnouf. He was Librarian at the École Normale Supérieure (~1864–1888), taught at the Sorbonne (1868), and held a post at EPHE (~1869–1890).
Eugénie Bazin-Foucher was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her studies at the Sorbonne and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1915–1918) under Sylvain Lévi.

Eugénie Sellers was a historian and archaeologist. She studied at Girton College, Cambridge (1879–1882) and the British School at Athens (1890–1891), later holding posts at Chatsworth House (1904–1908) and the British School at Rome (1909–1925).

Eun Hino is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2006). She was a project researcher at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2015) and held assistant and associate professor posts at Musashino University.
Keiun Maeda was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as president (学長) of Toyo University and as president of Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini, served as assistant professor at the University of Michigan until 2004, and became professor at Seoul National University.
Eunyoung Choe is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate from Korea University. She served as an HK professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2015).

Eustaquio Echauri Martínez was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Conciliar Seminary of Pamplona and Universidad Central. He was Professor of Latin at the University of Barcelona (1920) and Professor of Greek and Sanskrit at Complutense University (1940).
Eva De Clercq is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Ghent University (1999–2003) and held a post there as a permanent member in 2025.

Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She served as Professor and Chair of East Asian Studies at the University of Alberta and as Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary (attested 2006).
Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under the traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin and held a post at the University of Calgary (attested 1992).

Eva Tichy is a linguist and Indologist. She studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, completed her habilitation at the University of Marburg, and held the Chair of Indo-European Studies at the University of Freiburg (1993–2017).

Eva Wilden is an Indologist who completed her M.A., doctorate, and habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1985–2004). She served at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2003) and became a professor at the University of Hamburg in 2017.
